reason: On iOS opening, an exact stable daily copy can already protect the local board, yet cloud adoption tried to append the same full board again and could hit quota. The old failed-backup gate was strengthened with a genuinely unsaved local edit so it still proves a missing recovery copy blocks replacement. New tests cover malformed backup bytes, transactional markers, durable adoption, conditional union push, in-flight edits, and reload. An independent review found that deleting a visible backup rewrote only the filtered list and silently dropped an older unreadable recovery row. The new red-first tests require visible raw recovery and single-row deletion against the original stored index.
previousBehavior: Every cloud adoption appended another pre-adoption backup even when a stable exact copy existed. Quota could hold the cloud, and a later board-store failure could leave an adopted state unsaved or advance reconciliation bookkeeping. A held read from an earlier reconciled session could release a pending write. Settings hid expired malformed rows, then deleting another visible backup silently removed those hidden bytes.
intendedBehavior: Reuse only an exact stable recovery snapshot for cloud adoption; preserve distinct and unreadable backup bytes. Accept a replacement after its merged board reaches local storage. Permit only that exact saved board with its original stable snapshot to reach the cloud, persist its revision acknowledgement, and keep later edits behind the ordinary backup gate. Settings must show unreadable rows and offer exact raw view/download. An explicit deletion removes only one uniquely identified row, preserving other source bytes and refusing stale or ambiguous indices.
